title: Breast imaging

steps.tx: Standardised mammographic classification directs diagnostic and interventional workflows. The **BI-RADS** assessment categories span from 0 for incomplete evaluations requiring further imaging, to 1 for negative exams, through to 6 for confirmed biopsy-proven **malignancy** undergoing definitive management in clinical oncology practice.

rows: Additional imaging or prior film comparison

steps.tx: Category 4 lesions warrant histological evaluation due to intermediate malignancy risk. The **BI-RADS 4** category encompasses suspicious findings with risk spanning from 2% to 95%, subdivided into 4A with low suspicion (2% to 10%), 4B with intermediate suspicion (10% to 50%), and 4C with high suspicion of **malignancy** (50% to 95%).

steps.tx: Morphological patterns of mineral deposits reflect benign secretion versus aggressive intraductal necrosis. High-risk suspicious **microcalcifications** indicative of **ductal carcinoma in situ** include fine linear, branching, and fine pleomorphic calcifications distributed in a linear or segmental ductal distribution across the breast parenchyma.

steps.tx: Malignant epithelial neoplasms disrupt normal Cooper ligaments and surrounding parenchymal architecture. Classical **invasive ductal carcinoma** presents on screening mammography as a high-attenuation, irregular mass with radiating **spiculated margins**, appearing taller than wide with architectural distortion and retraction in the affected symptomatic breast.

steps.tx: Loss of E-cadherin expression permits infiltrative growth without creating discrete tissue borders. Consequently, **invasive lobular carcinoma** is characteristically subtle on mammography due to its single-file infiltrative architecture, often presenting only as subtle **architectural distortion** or shrinking breast sign without a discrete central mass.

steps.tx: Benign fibroepithelial neoplasms dominate in young reproductive-aged females. On ultrasound examination, a **fibroadenoma** appears as an oval or gently macrolobulated, well-circumscribed hypoechoic mass with a wider-than-tall orientation and uniform internal echoes, showing low **resistance index** on Doppler evaluation during examination.

steps.tx: Rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial neoplasms in women aged over 40 require histological differentiation from simple fibroadenomas. A **phyllodes tumour** appears as a large, rapidly growing mass resembling a fibroadenoma on imaging, distinguished histopathologically by cystic clefts and marked **stromal hypercellularity** on tissue biopsy specimens in adult patients.

steps.tx: Dynamic contrast-enhanced breast MRI evaluates tumour neoangiogenesis. Kinetic analysis classifies curves into Type 1 progressive persistent enhancement (typically benign), Type 2 plateau kinetics (intermediate), and Type 3 rapid wash-in with fast **wash-out kinetics**, strongly indicative of **malignancy** on dynamic sequences.
